newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains driven by currencies, EU tender.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains driven by currencies, EU tender.

text.p: LIFFE grain futures ended unchanged or firmer after a day of ups and downs inspired by currency moves and news ahead of and after the EU tender.

First the large scale of bids sent futures up, one trader said. Then disappointment at the actual award, combined with sterling getting off its lows against other European currencies, brought them back down.
The most active contract in wheat, May, last traded unchanged at 96.70 stg per tonne, on volume of 317 lots out of a total of 495.
May had seen a high of 97.75 earlier in the day as the bidding for the EU tender became known, the trader said.
He expressed disappointment at slow trade in the new crop, with just 17 lots of November changing hands.
Barley ended firm, with March, just the most active, last traded 0.25 stg up at 92.25 stg.
